title: When the Neutral fell, the hunting ground opened
summary: In the winter of 1650–51 Haudenosaunee war parties destroyed the Neutral Confederacy in Ontario, part of the shift that left Kentucky a contested hunting ground.
bodyMarkdown:
In the winter of 1650–51, after destroying the Huron towns, Haudenosaunee war parties overran the country of the Neutral (Attawandaron) in what is now southern Ontario. They burned villages and ended the Neutral Confederacy as a separate nation. It was one campaign in the [Beaver Wars](https://grokipedia.com/page/Beaver_Wars), covered more broadly in the [Iroquois Beaver Wars](/stories/iroquois-beaver-wars/) story.

With the Neutral, and soon the [Erie](/stories/erie-the-cat-nation/), broken, Iroquois power reached over the hunting ranges of former rivals. The upper Ohio Valley was left without large resident confederacies. In the following decades it was used as contested hunting ground, first by the Iroquois and later by the Shawnee, Cherokee, and others who moved into the gap.

That is one reason maps of Kentucky from the mid-1600s to the early 1700s read as hunting territory rather than a land of large permanent towns. The land was used, not empty.

## Kentucky today

These events took place in Ontario, so this story has no Kentucky map pin.
